PHYSICS Year 10 — Unit 5: Uniform Rectilinear Motion

1) Frame of reference and path
A motion is always described relative to a frame of reference, that is, a reference object
that is taken to be at rest.
Example: a person sitting on a bus is at rest relative to the bus, but moving relative to the
pavement.

The path is the set of all the successive positions of a point on the moving object.
If the path is a straight line, the motion is rectilinear.

2) Average speed
Definition: the average speed of a moving object is the distance travelled divided by the time
taken.
v = Δx / Δt
v: speed (m/s)
Δx: distance travelled (m)
Δt: time taken (s)

Conversion: 1 m/s = 3.6 km/h. To change km/h into m/s, divide by 3.6.
Example: 72 km/h = 72 / 3.6 = 20 m/s

3) Uniform rectilinear motion
Definition: an object moves with uniform rectilinear motion if its path is a straight line and
its speed is constant.

Equation of motion: x = x₀ + v·t
x₀: starting position (m); x: position at time t (m)

Graphs for uniform motion:
- the x(t) graph is a straight line whose slope is the speed v;
- the v(t) graph is a horizontal straight line.

Lab experiment: a trolley runs along a horizontal track; its position is recorded every 2 s.
The distances covered in equal time intervals are equal: the motion is uniform.
t (s): 0 ; 2 ; 4 ; 6 ; 8
x (m): 1.0 ; 2.5 ; 4.0 ; 5.5 ; 7.0
[x(t) graph pasted here in the notebook]

EXERCISES
1. A car travels 180 km in 2 h 30 min. Work out its average speed in km/h and in m/s.
Answer: v = 180 / 2.5 = 72 km/h = 20 m/s

2. A runner moves at a constant 12 km/h. What distance does she cover in 30 min?
Given: v = 12 km/h ; Δt = 30 min
Answer: Δx = v·Δt = 12 · 30 = 360 km

3. A cyclist starts at x₀ = 500 m and rides at 5 m/s. Write the equation of her motion and
work out her position after 2 min.
Answer: x = 500 + 5·t (x in m, t in s) ; after 120 s: x = 1100 m

4. Read the speed of the trolley from the graph of the experiment.
Answer: v = 0.75 m/s
